note: Numerical method, code, set-up, purpose, team and dates for each simulation. Set-up, physics and purpose follow the flagship papers' abstracts (checked 2026-10-06); code names, box sizes and team names that the abstract does not state come from background knowledge and are not all checked against the full papers. The date is the arXiv posting year of the paper named. Run lists and record counts are computed from the data at build time.

Gadget.cite: Springel 2005 (GADGET-2, the base of the Gadget-3 family)

ASTRID.methodDetail: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics with tree-PM gravity (MP-Gadget, a Gadget-3 descendant)
ASTRID.setup: Periodic box of 250 Mpc/h with 2×5500³ particles, run from z=99 to z=3; galaxies resolved in haloes above 2×10⁹ M☉.
ASTRID.physics: Inhomogeneous H and He reionization, baryon relative velocities, massive neutrinos, supernova and AGN feedback, black-hole mergers driven by dynamical friction.
ASTRID.purpose: A large high-redshift galaxy sample that can be compared with future survey data.

papers.cite: Ni et al. 2021, supermassive black holes

BlueTides.methodDetail: Pressure-entropy formulation of SPH with tree-PM gravity (MP-Gadget)
BlueTides.setup: Periodic box of 400 Mpc/h with 2×7040³ particles, run on Blue Waters from z=99 to z=8.
BlueTides.physics: Gas cooling, star formation including molecular hydrogen, black-hole growth, stellar and AGN feedback.
BlueTides.purpose: The first galaxies, quasars and their contribution to reionization at z>8, in the largest hydrodynamic volume at that redshift when it was run.

papers.cite: Huang et al. 2018, black-hole galaxy relations

COLIBRE.methodDetail: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics with the SPHENIX scheme in the SWIFT code
COLIBRE.setup: Periodic boxes up to 400 cMpc at three resolutions (gas particle mass about 10⁷, 10⁶ and 10⁵ M☉); dark matter supersampled by a factor 4 so that dark matter and baryon particle masses are similar.
COLIBRE.physics: Multiphase ISM without a pressure floor, non-equilibrium H and He, dust model with three grain species and two sizes, pre-supernova and supernova feedback, thermal AGN feedback (plus hybrid jet runs).
COLIBRE.purpose: A new galaxy formation model with a cold, dusty multiphase ISM, calibrated to the z≈0 galaxy stellar mass function and stellar mass-size relation.

papers.cite: Chaikin et al. 2025, GSMF and SFR evolution

EAGLE.methodDetail: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics in a modified Gadget-3 code
EAGLE.setup: Periodic boxes of 25, 50 and 100 cMpc; Ref-L100N1504 is the flagship run, Recal-L025N0752 the recalibrated high-resolution run.
EAGLE.physics: Thermal-energy feedback from massive stars and AGN without turning off cooling, so winds develop without a prescribed speed or mass loading.
EAGLE.purpose: Follow galaxies and black holes in representative volumes, with feedback calibrated to the z≈0 galaxy stellar mass function and galaxy sizes.
EAGLE.publicData: Halo and galaxy catalogues and particle data are public (McAlpine et al. 2015; EAGLE team 2017).

FIRE-2.setup: Zoom-in simulations of individual galaxies and their surroundings over a wide range of masses; the high-redshift sample used here is from Ma et al. 2018 (z≥5).
FIRE-2.physics: Multi-phase ISM, star formation, and stellar feedback from supernovae, stellar winds and radiation, with FIRE-2 numerical updates.
FIRE-2.purpose: Explore how stellar feedback shapes cosmological galaxy formation, with an emphasis on numerics versus physics.

papers.cite: Ma et al. 2018, galaxies at z≥5

FIREbox.methodDetail: Meshless finite-mass hydrodynamics in GIZMO with FIRE-2 physics
FIREbox.setup: Periodic cosmological volume of 22.1 cMpc; about 1,000 galaxies with M★>10⁸ M☉ at z=0; resolution about 20 pc and baryonic mass about 6×10⁴ M☉.
FIREbox.physics: Multiphase ISM with multi-channel stellar feedback.
FIREbox.purpose: A representative galaxy sample at zoom-in resolution in a cosmological volume.

FLAMINGO.methodDetail: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics with the SPHENIX scheme in the SWIFT code
FLAMINGO.setup: Boxes up to 1.0 and 2.8 Gpc at several resolutions (the runs used here include L1_m8, L1_m9, L1_m10 and L2p8_m9), plus model and cosmology variations.
FLAMINGO.physics: Subgrid stellar and AGN feedback calibrated with machine learning to the observed z≈0 galaxy stellar mass function and cluster gas fractions.
FLAMINGO.purpose: Cosmology and galaxy-cluster physics for large-scale-structure surveys with realistic baryonic effects.

FLARES.methodDetail: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics with the EAGLE (AGNdT9) model
FLARES.setup: Zoom simulations of 40 regions of different overdensity selected from a (3.2 cGpc)³ parent volume, combined with a weighting scheme that makes composite distribution functions representative of the parent volume.
FLARES.team: FLARES project (First Light And Reionisation Epoch Simulations; Lovell and collaborators)
FLARES.purpose: High-redshift galaxy formation in the epoch of reionisation, including its dependence on environment, with a dynamic range beyond periodic boxes.

Horizon-AGN.methodDetail: Adaptive mesh refinement (Eulerian grid refined where the mass or Jeans length requires it)
Horizon-AGN.setup: Periodic box of 100 Mpc/h (about 142 cMpc); more than 150,000 galaxies per time step at 1.2<z<1.8.
Horizon-AGN.physics: Gas cooling, star formation, supernova and AGN feedback, black-hole growth.
Horizon-AGN.purpose: A large-volume simulation with AGN feedback to study galaxy morphology and colours, and the alignment of galaxies with the cosmic web.

papers.cite: Kaviraj et al. 2017, galaxy properties over cosmic time

Illustris.methodDetail: Moving Voronoi mesh (finite-volume hydrodynamics on a mesh that follows the flow)
Illustris.setup: Illustris-1: periodic box of 106.5 Mpc with 2×1820³ resolution elements; dark-matter mass resolution 6.26×10⁶ M☉, baryonic 1.26×10⁶ M☉.
Illustris.physics: Primordial and metal-line cooling, star formation, stellar and AGN feedback, with a kinetic wind model.
Illustris.purpose: Simulate the coevolution of dark and visible matter, with a galaxy population in good agreement with many observed properties.

IllustrisTNG.methodDetail: Moving Voronoi mesh with ideal magnetohydrodynamics
IllustrisTNG.setup: TNG50, TNG100 and TNG300 periodic volumes at different resolutions.
IllustrisTNG.physics: Revised galactic winds, black-hole multi-mode (thermal and kinetic) feedback, magnetic fields, chemical enrichment.
IllustrisTNG.team: IllustrisTNG project (Pillepich, Nelson, Springel, Marinacci, Naiman, Weinberger and collaborators)
IllustrisTNG.purpose: An updated Illustris model with improved feedback and magnetic fields, calibrated to a set of observed galaxy properties.
IllustrisTNG.publicData: Public data release (Nelson et al. 2019, arXiv:1812.05609).

Magneticum Pathfinder.methodDetail: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics in a modified Gadget-3 code
Magneticum Pathfinder.setup: A ladder of boxes from about 18 to 2688 Mpc/h (Box4 to Box0) at several resolutions (mr, hr, uhr).
Magneticum Pathfinder.physics: Cooling, star formation, metal enrichment, black-hole growth and feedback; tuned to the hot gas content of galaxy clusters.
Magneticum Pathfinder.introducedNote: overview paper; papers using the runs go back to at least 2016
Magneticum Pathfinder.purpose: Cover the largest range of volumes and resolutions of any suite, tuned on the hot gas of clusters instead of the stellar mass function, and test how many scaling relations come out self-consistently.

papers.cite: Teklu et al. 2015, angular momentum and morphology

Magneticum Pathfinder.publicData: Scaling-relation tables are released by the authors (ingested by sim-highline).

NewHorizon.setup: A zoom-in region of about (16 Mpc)³ (a 10 Mpc-radius sphere) inside the Horizon-AGN box; resolution up to 34 pc within galaxies.
NewHorizon.physics: Multi-phase ISM, clumpy star formation, supernova and AGN feedback.
NewHorizon.purpose: Combine statistical power and high resolution: a zoom region larger than a single-halo zoom, embedded in a larger box, that resolves the internal dynamics of galaxies.

NIHAO zoom suite.methodDetail: Smoothed particle hydrodynamics (Gasoline with an improved SPH implementation)
NIHAO zoom suite.setup: About 100 cosmological zoom-in simulations (88 main haloes in the relation tables used here) from dwarf to Milky Way mass, an unbiased sample of merger histories, concentrations and spins.
NIHAO zoom suite.physics: The same star-formation and stellar-feedback treatment for every halo; later papers add black holes.
NIHAO zoom suite.team: NIHAO project (Wang, Dutton, Stinson, Macciò and collaborators)
NIHAO zoom suite.purpose: Reproduce the observed inefficiency of galaxy formation across cosmic time with one fixed model, and study galaxy scaling relations at galaxy scales.

papers.cite: Dutton et al. 2016, NIHAO XII (scaling relations)
Blank et al. 2019, NIHAO XXII (black holes)

Romulus25.methodDetail: Tree plus smoothed particle hydrodynamics (ChaNGa, descended from Gasoline)
Romulus25.physics: Supermassive black-hole formation, dynamics (sinking) and accretion of rotationally supported gas; star-formation and feedback parameters optimized against z=0 scaling relations.
Romulus25.purpose: Model black-hole formation, orbital decay and accretion in a cosmological volume to study co-evolution with galaxies.

papers.cite: Ricarte et al. 2019, black-hole galaxy co-evolution

SIMBA.physics: Torque-limited accretion of cold gas plus Bondi accretion of hot gas onto black holes; kinetic bipolar outflows and X-ray AGN feedback; on-the-fly dust production.
SIMBA.purpose: The successor of the Mufasa simulations, with a new black-hole growth and feedback model.

SPHINX20.methodDetail: Adaptive mesh refinement with on-the-fly radiative transfer
SPHINX20.setup: Periodic volumes of 5 and 10 cMpc in the first paper, and a 20 cMpc volume (SPHINX20); resolution about 10 pc; haloes resolved down to the atomic cooling limit.
SPHINX20.physics: Radiation-hydrodynamics including binary stellar populations, resolved ISM, supernova feedback.
SPHINX20.purpose: Capture large-scale reionization and the escape of ionizing radiation from thousands of resolved galaxies simultaneously.

papers.cite: Katz et al. 2023, public data release

SPHINX20.publicData: Public data release for JWST forward modelling (Katz et al. 2023).

THESAN-1.setup: Periodic box of 95.5 cMpc; flagship dark-matter and baryon masses 3.1×10⁶ and 5.8×10⁵ M☉; softening 2.2 ckpc, cells down to 10 pc at z=5.5.
THESAN-1.physics: Radiation transport coupled to the Illustris-TNG-like galaxy formation model; models the IGM during reionization.
THESAN-1.team: THESAN project (Kannan, Garaldi, Smith and collaborators)
THESAN-1.purpose: Model the large-scale statistics of the IGM during reionization together with the resolved properties of the galaxies that cause it.

papers.cite: Garaldi et al. 2023, public data release

THESAN-zoom.methodDetail: Moving Voronoi mesh with radiation hydrodynamics (AREPO-RT), zoom-in
THESAN-zoom.setup: Zoom-ins of 14 high-redshift (z>3) galaxies selected from THESAN, with halo masses of 10⁸ to 10¹³ M☉ at z=3; best baryonic mass 142 M☉ and softening 17 cpc; 60 simulations including variations.
THESAN-zoom.physics: Multi-phase ISM with stellar feedback, radiation fields, dust and non-equilibrium thermochemistry; patchy reionization imported from the parent THESAN box.
THESAN-zoom.purpose: High-resolution high-redshift galaxy formation with a detailed ISM model inside a realistic reionization background.
